newsitem.title: FINLAND: PENOPE TO BUY KONTRAM FOR FIM 96 MLN.
newsitem.headline: PENOPE TO BUY KONTRAM FOR FIM 96 MLN.

text.p: Finnish mechanical wood industry machine importer Penope Oy said on Tuesday it had signed a preliminary agreement to buy trading company Kontram-Yhtiot for 96 million markka.
"The acquisition will be mainly financed with a directed share issue," it said in a statement.

"Penope's board proposes to a shareholders' meeting to be held on June 19, 1997 that the share capital be raised through a directed share issue of at least 2,775,300 markka and a maximum 5,500,000 markka," it said.
In the issue, up to 555,060 shares would be issued to Kontram's owner managing director Arto Jokinen and a maxmimum 1.1 million shares would go to institutions.
Penope said the deal was aimed to "develop the group in the technical equipment trading sector in the Nordic countries, Baltics and nearby areas in Russia".
"Financing mostly with equity and the aggregate cashflow of the companies will maintain the future Penope group's equity-to-assets ratio and debt servicing capacity at a good level," it said.
It said Kontram's net sales in 1996 were 167.9 million markka, up from 121.4 million in 1995, and its profit before taxes rose to 24.5 million from 17.6 million in 1995.
Penope's 1996 net sales were 89.4 million markka versus 87.6 in 1995 and its pretax profit was 1.2 million markka, down from 4.8 million.
